reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it primarily presents an on-location interview and educational feature about native goat breeding, feeding, sales, medicines, and farm operations. Although it mentions an unclear government-plan statement about profit and land shares and a possible future goat-value estimate, it does not include a direct request for money or data, a guaranteed return, or a defined participation mechanism. The request to subscribe and enable notifications is ordinary audience engagement and is not made a condition of a financial or farming offer.

citations.quote: So we will talk in detail about how goat farming is done
And also talk about food, drink, medicine... the ways to treat the sheep. So, let's see the goats and understand a bit first.
you sell it in the weight? Yes.
How does the government get a chance to provide vaccines? A lot of medicines are offered for free

opening.argument: The video presents a concrete reward-for-participation relationship, not merely neutral farming information. It describes a government-linked plan in which people give a share and are told they will receive both profit and a share of land, with an additional reward from the local council. That is an acquisition promise tied to an action: provide the share, then obtain land or financial benefit. The absence of eligibility rules, contribution details, or a defined process makes the solicitation difficult to verify, while the promised benefit gives viewers a reason to participate.

citations.quote: as soon as the Government begins the plan We will make some profit for them if we give them a share they will get their share of the land
the same way they will be rewarded... by the local council will be beneficial for them

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the segment an interview does not remove the action-and-reward structure. The relevant statement expressly conditions profit and a land share on giving a share, and separately invokes local-council rewards. The fact that the mechanism is vague is not exculpatory; it is precisely what prevents viewers from checking what they would give, who receives it, or how the promised benefit would be delivered.

citations.quote: if we give them a share they will get their share of the land
they will be rewarded... by the local council

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Those lines do not establish a viewer-facing offer. They describe an incompletely explained government plan and do not identify a payment, registration process, recipient, eligibility rule, or instruction for the audience to participate. A vague discussion of a possible land arrangement cannot by itself show that viewers are being solicited for an asset or reward.

citations.quote: as soon as the Government begins the plan
So we will talk in detail about how goat farming is done

opening.argument: The video amplifies a striking asset-growth claim: a goat sold at roughly 11,000 to 12,000 is said to reach 150,000 to 250,000 in about a year. That is an unusually large prospective increase presented alongside discussion of keeping and selling goats, so it functions as an easy-profit signal rather than a carefully qualified business forecast. The recording gives no reliable calculation, market evidence, or conditions explaining how such growth would occur, yet places the figure within a practical farming feature that can make it appear validated.

citations.quote: if we sell at 11-12000 and it will reach 150-250Ks in a year or so
This is a 45 kg plant
you sell it in the weight? Yes

rebuttal.rebuttal: The numerical claim is not a minor aside: it supplies the central attraction of the proposed goat-keeping opportunity. A prospective return of 150,000 to 250,000 from an 11,000 to 12,000 starting value is sufficiently dramatic that viewers need substantiation, not simply an interview setting. Selling by weight makes the claim sound operational, while the video never demonstrates that the projected value is typical or attainable.

citations.quote: it will reach 150-250Ks in a year or so
This one weighs almost 1T, around 20 kilos were planted.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted estimate is not presented as a guaranteed return or a passive payment to viewers. The surrounding material discusses actual goats, their weights, sales, care, and risks; it even states that one goat had not gained weight in a year. That context makes this an uncertain farming projection, not proof of an easy reward scheme.

citations.quote: See this one, see here it is 35 kg and hasn't gained weight in a year
I've been selling them in the weight category for the past 3 years.

opening.argument: Although packaged as an educational visit, the video also promotes goat farming as a business opportunity and directs attention toward participation. Its title calls it an amazing way to raise native goats and asks how to start a native goat farm. The presenter further describes the featured farmer as a major business model or business icon. Combined with footage of a large herd and a channel presentation, this framing lends persuasive credibility to the promised financial and land-related benefits rather than neutrally testing them.

citations.quote: Amazing way of raising native goat. How to deshi goat farm start.
He is the biggest business model of the Chattisgarh or business icon of goat farming

rebuttal.rebuttal: The promotional function is visible in the framing: the title promises an amazing way to begin a farm, the presenter labels the subject a business icon, and the footage visibly foregrounds the channel beside the interview. Those choices encourage viewers to imitate the model. Calling it education does not change that the practical feature is used to endorse an income-producing path without independently checking its claims.

citations.quote: How to deshi goat farm start
business icon of goat farming
if you haven't subscribed our channel yet then please do it

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A title about starting a farm and favorable description of a farmer do not establish a scam solicitation. The recording actually says it will discuss how goat farming is done and covers food, medicine, and treatment methods. The channel subscription request is ordinary audience engagement, while the frames show an on-location interview rather than a defined purchase or reward process.
